source.title: Resa: Transparent Reasoning Models via SAEs
source.authors: Shangshang Wang; Julian Asilis; Ömer Faruk Akgül; E. Bilgin; Ollie Liu; Deqing Fu; Willie Neiswanger

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper uses SAEs to identify and count prompt-defined features in language-model activations, providing an indirect test of whether SAE dictionaries can recover sparse features in LLMs. It does not test superposition geometry or capacity competition.
record.gate_note: The paper reports feature counts by SAE hookpoint and a distributional comparison with reasoning scores. The reported benchmark results for SAE-tuned models are not rows for the claim versions because they measure reasoning performance, not superposition or feature recoverability. The paper's standard-SFT comparisons concern its training method, not the claim.
record.test_reason: The paper uses SAEs as a tool to transfer reasoning ability (SAE-Tuning) and mainly reports benchmark performance. Its 'reasoning feature' counts come from a selection rule: SAE latents firing only at <think> and </think> in one system prompt. Those counts are 0–5 out of 65,536 latents. They do not measure whether features are spread across neurons, whether a dictionary recovers sparse features in general, or anything about capacity or geometry. No version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SAE-Tuning on CoT-free data elicits reasoning matching RL-trained models at much lower cost, and that the extracted abilities generalize out of distribution and work as modular adapters. They also conclude that prompt-selected 'reasoning features' follow a tri-modal layer distribution whose GMM structure correlates with performance, while single-layer counts are not predictive. They make no claim about superposition.
record.recipe_differences: The cited original studies toy networks and superposition geometry; this paper trains and uses SAEs on transformer activations and counts prompt-defined reasoning features.
record.method_sensitivity: The identified feature count varies by SAE hookpoint; four tested layers have a count of 0.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 26 per-layer SAE-Tuned models, 3-component GMM fits to think-token-only feature counts and to benchmark scores have similar means (4.9/14.5/22.7 vs 5.6/15.1/23.0) and weights. Per-layer counts do not predict per-layer scores: layer 18 has 0 features and the top score.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The layer distribution of prompt-selected SAE latents roughly tracks the layer distribution of SAE-Tuning performance, though single-layer counts do not predict it.

record.problems: Feature recovery is assessed using the authors' prompt-only definition and is not independently validated as causal or complete. Feature counts are reported without uncertainty estimates. The reported feature-count experiment is confined to Tina-STILL and the specified prompt procedure.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. The per-layer reasoning benchmark scores in Table 6 were not entered as rows because they measure reasoning performance after SAE-Tuning, not feature recoverability or superposition.

untested.parts: No toy models, overlap, orthogonality, sparsity transition or geometry.
No test of capacity competition or importance-based allocation.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Neither distributed coding across neurons nor dictionary recoverability of sparse features is measured. Counts of latents passing a think-token-only filter are a selection step, not a recovery test.
No test of completeness, stability or canonicality of SAE features. Pretrained, fine-tuned and from-scratch SAEs are compared only on downstream benchmark scores.

record.verdict_notes: The reader marked this T2 'tests' on V4. It is T4: the SAE is a tool, and the feature counts are outputs of a selection rule, not evidence about superposition or feature recovery. There are internal inconsistencies: the Table 6 caption attributes counts to Tina-STILL while the GMM text says base model; the default hookpoint is stated as layer 12, but Resa-STILL-v1's scores (47.28) match the '13th-Layer' row. No uncertainty estimates are reported, and the benchmark rows rest on 30-question AIME sets.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks, feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether polysemanticity results from competition for limited capacity or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemanticity is evidence for superposition.

The feature-count experiment is limited to reasoning features under a particular think-token prompt and SAE procedure. It does not establish that features are spread across many neurons, that the identified features are complete, or that the findings generalize across LLMs.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of the model.
Does not test whether features are intrinsically one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.
